title: Brand-new prototype pollution gadget in MongoDB leading to RCE

preconditions: JavaScript code merges/clones user-controlled objects using a recursive merge that does not block __proto__/constructor.prototype keys

process.action: Identify client- or server-side JS code paths that merge user input into an object (deep merge, clone, JSON parse into config)
process.expected_observation: Recursive merge/assign function reachable with attacker-controlled keys

process.action: Submit a payload with a __proto__ or constructor.prototype key to attempt polluting Object.prototype
process.expected_observation: A new property appears on all objects (e.g. {}.polluted === 'yes')

process.action: Identify a gadget that consumes the polluted property in a security-sensitive way (e.g. an isAdmin default, template rendering flag)
process.expected_observation: Application behavior changes based on the polluted global property

process.action: Chain the pollution with the identified gadget to achieve a concrete impact (privilege escalation, XSS, DoS)
process.expected_observation: Concrete security impact (e.g. unauthorized admin UI rendered) confirmed

impact: Denial of service via crashing application logic
Privilege escalation or XSS when a polluted property is consumed by a security-relevant gadget
remediation: Use Object.create(null) or Map for user-controlled key/value storage instead of plain objects
Use merge/clone libraries that explicitly block __proto__, constructor, and prototype keys
Freeze Object.prototype in sensitive contexts where feasible
